questions.q: What does Ops's actual ask from Lesson 1 translate to on this page?
options: A count of orders by status, to see where orders are piling up
A revenue total by payment method
A list of customer names
A map of order delivery locations
questions.explain: Ops asked specifically for order counts broken out by status — this page's core deliverable.

questions.q: Why does `[Order Count]` use `DISTINCTCOUNT(order_id)` instead of `COUNTROWS(fct_orders)`?
options: DISTINCTCOUNT stays correct even if fct_orders ever has more than one row for the same order_id; COUNTROWS would silently inflate
DISTINCTCOUNT is always faster to compute than COUNTROWS
COUNTROWS doesn't work on fact tables
There's no real difference between the two for this model
questions.explain: This is the deliberate safeguard: a plain row count would inflate if duplicate order_id rows ever existed, while DISTINCTCOUNT would not.

questions.q: What does the `Orders Stuck` measure count?
options: Orders not marked completed, placed more than seven days ago
All orders placed in the current month
Orders with a null customer_id
Orders where the payment amount is zero
questions.explain: It's an operational alert: CALCULATE with status <> "completed" and a DATEDIFF filter past 7 days.

questions.q: Why does the sanity check matter more on this page than on Finance's revenue page?
options: A mismatch here means Ops is told the wrong number of orders exist — more immediately visible than dollars being slightly off
This page has no sanity check available
Finance's page doesn't need to be correct, only this one does
DISTINCTCOUNT cannot be checked against Snowflake directly
questions.explain: A wrong order count is a more immediately obvious kind of wrong than a revenue figure that's off by a smaller, less visible margin.

questions.q: What Snowflake query checks `[Order Count]` directly?
options: `select count(distinct order_id) from fct_orders`
`select count(*) from fct_orders`
`select sum(amount) from fct_orders`
`select avg(order_id) from fct_orders`
questions.explain: Matching DISTINCTCOUNT's own logic, the Snowflake check counts distinct order_id values, not raw rows.
